english: don’t count your chickens before they are hatched
also: don’t count your chickens before they hatch

terms.latin: Adhūc tua messis in herbā est.
evidence: Ov. Her. 17.263: sed nimium properās, et adhūc tua messis in herbā est (Lewis & Short s.v. messis)
terms.comment: Literally “your harvest is still in the blade”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
